question: Which wastewater plants should Horton call first?
html:
Horton should call New Haven East Shore, Hartford and Norwalk first. Each has a project on Connecticut's fundable list plus a larger request behind it. MWRA Deer Island and Bridgeport Westside come next (CET wastewater-plant targets).

First five calls

RankPlantHorton fitFundable or listed projectFollow-on request
1New Haven East Shore STP (40 MGD)98$82M wet-weather/odor-control upgrade, CT FY27 fundable list$19.2M process-air compressors
2Hartford WPCF (60 MGD, CT's largest)96$24.3M sludge screening and equalization, FY26-27$31.6M Island Road and Hog Brook pump stations
3Norwalk WPCF (18 MGD)95$26M final-settling-tank upgrade, FY27$48M green aeration system
4MWRA Deer Island (MA)94$289M Clarifier #2, 2026 IUPStorage and efficiency, not solar
5Bridgeport Westside WPCA (30 MGD)93Project detail truncated in the extract—

All figures are from the CET wastewater-plant targets list, generated Sep 24, 2026.

Why this order

  • The top three are in Horton's home state. The growth plan names them as the lead targets among 62 funded or requested projects across CT, MA and RI (CET growth plan).
  • Norwalk is the best NuWave pairing. Aeration is the plant's largest energy load, so electrical and efficiency work can be sold together.
  • Deer Island already self-generates 26% of its power. Lead with electrical subcontracting and storage.
  • Pipeline value is $105.7M at Hartford and $76.5M at Norwalk. New Haven's figure is cut off in the extract.

Funding caveat

  • The follow-on requests ($19.2M, $31.6M, $48M) are Connecticut Table 3 items. Those are eligible only for first-come reserves and are not on the fundable list (CET wastewater-plant targets).
  • Rhode Island figures come from the June 2026 draft list. Only Table 2 items are proposed for funding.

Plant condition signals

These are context for the sales conversation, not compliance findings.

  • Bridgeport Westside: 12 quarters with noncompliance, one significant. Last inspection was Nov 20, 2024. The permit is administratively continued (EPA wastewater-plant compliance).
  • Hartford and New Haven: both permits are administratively continued. They expired Sep 30, 2020 and Feb 28, 2021.
  • Norwalk: the permit expired Mar 31, 2026 (CET wastewater-plant targets).

Older permits and repeat noncompliance may point to near-term capital needs (est.). Bid timing would confirm it.

Gaps to close

  • Bridgeport Westside's project and dollar value.
  • New Haven's full pipeline value.
  • Bid and procurement dates for each fundable project. These would set the call sequence more precisely than fit scores.

Next actions

  1. Pull procurement calendars and engineer-of-record names for New Haven, Hartford and Norwalk. Assign a Horton owner to each before year-end.
  2. Build a joint Horton electrical and NuWave aeration-efficiency pitch for Norwalk.
  3. Recover the truncated Bridgeport Westside and New Haven fields from the full target list.
  4. Cross-check ranks 6-15 against the Nov 23, 2026 compliance snapshot to queue the second wave.
